visualReview.notes: Actually inspected 89 final images: 16 portable, 16 shared, 32 medium-fi and 25 signed terrain views. Compared actual official illustrated plan, 1854 Stüler north/west design elevations and 2005 courtyard photograph. Horseshoe palace, distinct round and square tower forms, roofless court, pale St Michael and separate Christ chapel, dormers, crenellations, two open gates and three stacked ramp loops remain recognizable. Fresh entrance nodes differ from original map evidence; derivative gates now follow the covered-road centers and tangents. Geometry testing exposed an upper support blocking the lower entrance and visual terrain inspection exposed excavation gaps; both were corrected before final captures. A small bounded below-deck floor and retaining faces close the low-road cut. Original architectural interpretation, window counts, gate envelopes and vault shapes remain approximate; museum rooms, forested mountain, ivy, statuary, water tower and parking are outside this exterior scope.

sharedSurfaceReview.notes: Six common material graphs provide granite foundation, sandstone walls, limestone chapel, timber, painted metal and slate. Carved details share tinted sandstone. Opaque PBR glass and garden tint use two local slots without images; slate courses use the common graph rather than duplicate roof-course geometry. All six GLBs contain zero images. Actual shared images show coherent warm masonry, pale chapel and slate roofs. Each graph is read once and unloading releases model geometry. Skyline uses baked common linear material means in one draw. The shared geographic fixture is flat and cannot establish mountainous ground contact; the retained numeric terrain fixture independently covers that fit. Reference photographs are not redistributed.

mediumFiReview.notes: All 32 final style images inspected: noon and late light, economy/high modes, twelve architecture cameras, four whole-model levels and transitions. Skyline keeps separate tower forms, court, chapels, open gates, loop terraces and bounded excavation at 998 triangles. District adds shared surfaces at 3269 triangles; street restores facade openings and major ornament at 12161; close-up adds mullions, trim, tiled graph detail, crenellations and timber bridge planks at 43413. Small details fade with distance while the major silhouette and material means remain consistent. Synthetic surrounding buildings and low-mounted review ground are style context, not geographic evidence. Strict medium-fi reports no findings.

The derivative uses fresh coordinates without mirroring or rescaling. Retained public numeric terrain supplies 4225 samples on a 4 m native grid, with decoded anchor working datum 835.9281 m. Rigid -10.4563 m source shift fits the mapped approach to grade plus 0.08 m. Court is 19.5437 m above the working anchor. Structural skirts extend below retained grade.

fidelityReview.notes: Accepted medium-fi castle and multilevel entrance reconstruction. Original 349299-triangle, 30044980-byte master remains independently reproducible at sha256:5cb6e4124350dee11d4dd9368b9ae214494f141b73d15c7d050fcf08c45838e7 from unchanged hohenzollern-castle-model.mjs#hohenzollernStudy.build and original map-parts.json. Original evidence is retained alongside the independent current derivative. Official plan is illustrative, 1854 drawing is a design and 2005 photograph is a dated courtyard view; none is a measured current elevation. Temporary restoration scaffolding is omitted. Terrain pixel spacing is sampling spacing, not verified native DEM resolution or vertical accuracy; coarse data may include vegetation/buildings. Gate body dimensions, vaults, floor rise, supports, facade niches and fine decoration are interpreted. Physical-device timing and fit to arbitrary host terrain remain unmeasured.

legacyFidelityScope.notes: Maximum fidelity pending: no as-built measured elevations were available. Palace heights, roof ridges, tower crowns, dormers, window modules and chapel details are architectural reconstructions from references. The original 1854 elevations are design drawings rather than a current measured survey. The courtyard photograph is from 2005; the model excludes temporary modern scaffolding and does not claim a surveyed 2026 state. Spiral road centerlines and covered layers are mapped, but ramp gradients, retaining wall thickness, vault shapes and gate clearances are estimated. Supporting skirts are provisional; actual rock contour, grade and terrain contact remain unfinished. The forested mountain, distant water tower, parking buildings, vegetation/ivy, statuary, museum interiors and inaccessible casemates are outside this exterior asset. Shared sandstone, raw limestone, limestone, granite, slate, wood and painted metal surfaces carry exterior materials; no embedded photographs. Procedural masonry joints and slate courses are approximations.

geometryValidation.notes: Three focused tests pass: exact original bytes reproduce; current source/runtime and retained input hashes agree; signed fresh frame is accepted. All four browser levels pass both gate passages at three lateral positions, the actual curved lower route segments and sampled exposed western platform front faces at grade. Child-process browser rebuilds are byte-identical and meet 1000/4000/16000/64000 triangles, eight draws and 3 MB initial download. POSITION and NORMAL use separate 12-byte streams. Six GLBs pass Khronos with zero errors, warnings and images. Five normal-placement states sample the anchor once with zero model-origin offset within 0.1 mm. Independent triangular ground probes differ only by the 0.015 m fixture offset. Ground cut is active while mounted; five unloads restore ground and leave zero model geometries. These are targeted probes and rendered checks, not an exhaustive manifold or measured architectural survey.

terrainReview.notes: Actually inspected 25 final terrain images after opening the upper-ramp support crossing and closing the bounded excavation with a below-deck floor and inward retaining faces. Both gates and curved lower approach remain usable at all browser levels. The close Eagle camera follows a straight gate axis; the actual approach bends, so a retaining corner enters the right foreground. Explicit mapped-route rays pass. Coarse terrain and interpreted vertical layout remain accepted limits. Signed normal renderer, real heading, retained height reference, sampled exterior feet, both gate passages and cut lifecycle are recorded in the hash-bound report. Lower approach continuity is checked against the actual curved source paths, not the extrapolated camera axis. Civil supports fit this retained coarse product; actual elevations and universal host-terrain fit remain unverified.
